successors.name: Haryanka dynasty
successors.text: Magadha with Anga: Cliopatria's Haryanka row (-500..-405) opens at 33,403 km2 over the Magadha core and the Anga country (bbox 84.51-87.77E, 24.20-25.87N); drawn here as the corrected Patna-Gaya…

ledger.x: c. 600 BCE: Magadha, ruled from Rajagriha, appears as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the 'Patna and Gaya districts', bounded by the Ganga, Son and Campā. The page dates no founding ('the legendary Brihadratha dynasty was the first ruling dynasty of Magadha'); -600 is Cliopatria's start, so the date is a bridge.…
Early 6th century BCE: Anga and Magadha fight over Magadha.
544: Bimbisara founds the Haryanka dynasty at Rajagriha.
543 BCE: Bimbisara takes the Magadhan throne ('r.

c. 530 BCE: Bimbisara annexes Anga. 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara.' / 'This was the one and only conquest of Bimbisara.' The Magadha page agrees without a date ('Magadha expanded to include most of Bihar and Bengal with the conquest of Vajjika League and Anga, respectively'). The Bimbisara page…

c. 530 BCE: the stretch of the Ganga's south bank between the Patna-Gaya core and the annexed Anga country is drawn as Magadha's. The Magadha page has the Campā as Magadha's eastern border ('bounded to the north, west, and east respectively by the Gaṅgā, Son, and Campā rivers'), so Magadha and Anga touch; no page…
501 BCE: the Janapada of Magadha row ends and Cliopatria's Haryanka row (33,403 km2, from -500) takes the same land.

wars.name: Anga's war on Magadha
wars.outcome: Anga under Brahmadatta defeated Bimbisara's father; Bimbisara, on the throne from 543, later 'led a military campaign against Anga, perhaps to avenge his father's earlier defeat'.

wars.name: Bimbisara's conquest of Anga
wars.outcome: Magadha annexes Anga: 'Anga was annexed by Magadha in the time of Bimbisara'; 'This was the one and only conquest of Bimbisara.'

certainty.note: The pages give rivers, not lines: the Ganga to the north, the Son to the west and the Campa to the east; the Anga frontier after -530 is the Campa river, undated and approximate.
